messages.subject: question about 'group'
parts:
Could I persuade someone to explain (or point me to an explanation of) the formal statistical model that results from adding a 'group' argument to an f-specification?

Consider for example

y~f(time, model="ar1", group=mygroup, ...)

The addition of the 'group' argument adds a hyperparameter

GroupRho for 'time'

to the model summary. I understand the other two hyperparameters --- they're well explained in the ar1 help --- but I don't see where the GroupRho comes from. What's the statistical model being estimated here?

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about 'group'
parts:
there is an introduction here. it is just a kroecker product model. the
'group model' is constructed to have fixed variance 1, so there is no
variance inflation.

here are the available ones

> names(inla.models()$group)
[1] "exchangeable" "exchangeablepos"
"ar1" "ar"
[5]
"rw1" "rw2" "besag" "iid"
and their spesification is in

f(..., control.group = ...)

see ?control.group



we really should have a tutorial document on this, agree...

H
